    (durationDensity : ℝ → ℝ)
    (durationDensity_source :
      ContinuousDurationDensitySourceCondition durationDensity)
    {observedRate : ℝ}
    (observedRate_pos : 0 < observedRate)
    (retention_one_pos :
      0 < continuousDurationFirstReportProbability 1 durationDensity)
    (retention_two_pos :
      0 < continuousDurationFirstReportProbability 2 durationDensity) :
    ∃ reportingRate1 reportingRate2 : ℝ,
      0 < reportingRate1 ∧
      0 < reportingRate2 ∧
      reportingRate1 ≠ reportingRate2 ∧
      ∃ (Omega1 : Type) (mOmega1 : MeasurableSpace Omega1) (P1 : Measure Omega1)
          (M1 : @Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega1 mOmega1 P1),
        ∃ (Omega2 : Type) (mOmega2 : MeasurableSpace Omega2) (P2 : Measure Omega2)
            (M2 : @Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega2 mOmega2 P2),
          M1.reportingRate = reportingRate1 ∧
          M2.reportingRate = reportingRate2 ∧
          M1.observedIncidentRate = observedRate ∧
          M2.observedIncidentRate = observedRate ∧
          (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1,
            Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
              (M1.observedUniqueIncidentCount n omega : ℝ) / n)
              atTop (nhds observedRate)) ∧
          (∀ᵐ omega ∂P2,
            Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
              (M2.observedUniqueIncidentCount n omega : ℝ) / n)
              atTop (nhds observedRate)) ∧
          ((∀ t : ℝ≥0, Measurable (M1.markedProcess.observedCount t)) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1, M1.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1,
              Monotone fun t => M1.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) ∧
            ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M1.markedProcess.observedCount P1 ∧
            ∀ {s t : ℝ≥0}, s ≤ t → ∀ observedCount : ℕ,
              P1.real {omega : Omega1 |
                M1.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -
                  M1.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =
                countLikelihood
                  (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate
                    M1.incidentRate M1.reportingRate M1.durationDensity)
                  ((t : ℝ) - (s : ℝ)) observedCount) ∧
          ((∀ t : ℝ≥0, Measurable (M2.markedProcess.observedCount t)) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P2, M2.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P2,
              Monotone fun t => M2.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) ∧
            ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M2.markedProcess.observedCount P2 ∧
            ∀ {s t : ℝ≥0}, s ≤ t → ∀ observedCount : ℕ,
              P2.real {omega : Omega2 |
                M2.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -
                  M2.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =
                countLikelihood
                  (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate
                    M2.incidentRate M2.reportingRate M2.durationDensity)
                  ((t : ℝ) - (s : ℝ)) observedCount) := by
  refine ⟨1, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  rcases proposition1_steady_state_duration_source durationDensity
      durationDensity_source (by norm_num) observedRate_pos retention_one_pos
        (ContinuousDurationDensitySourceCondition.firstReportProbability_le_one
          durationDensity_source 1)
        retention_two_pos
        (ContinuousDurationDensitySourceCondition.firstReportProbability_le_one
          durationDensity_source 2) with
    ⟨hrates, Omega1, mOmega1, P1, M1, Omega2, mOmega2, P2, M2,
      hreporting1, hreporting2, hobserved1, hobserved2, hlln1, hlln2,
      observedProcess1, observedProcess2, hcount1, hcount2, hprocessRate⟩
  exact ⟨hrates, Omega1, mOmega1, P1, M1, Omega2, mOmega2, P2, M2,
    hreporting1, hreporting2, hobserved1, hobserved2, hlln1, hlln2,
    lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_observed_process M1,
    lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_observed_process M2⟩

    "effective_lean_source_declaration": "theorem lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_observed_process\n    {Omega : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega] {P : Measure Omega}\n    (M : Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega P) :\n    (\u2200 t : \u211d\u22650, Measurable (M.markedProcess.observedCount t)) \u2227\n      (\u2200\u1d50 omega \u2202P, M.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) \u2227\n      (\u2200\u1d50 omega \u2202P,\n        Monotone fun t => M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) \u2227\n      ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M.markedProcess.observedCount P \u2227\n      \u2200 {s t : \u211d\u22650}, s \u2264 t \u2192 \u2200 observedCount : \u2115,\n        P.real {omega : Omega |\n          M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -\n            M.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =\n          countLikelihood\n            (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate\n              M.incidentRate M.reportingRate M.durationDensity)\n            ((t : \u211d) - (s : \u211d)) observedCount := by\n  refine \u27e8M.markedProcess.observedCount_measurable,\n    M.markedProcess.observedCount_zero_ae,\n    M.markedProcess.observedCount_mono_ae,\n    M.markedProcess.observedCount_hasIndepIncrements, ?_\u27e9\n  intro s t hst observedCount\n  simpa [continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate,\n    M.latent_rate_eq_incidentRate,\n    M.retention_probability_eq_firstReportProbability] using\n    M.markedProcess.observedIntervalCount_mass_eq_countLikelihood hst observedCount",

theorem lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_observed_process
    {Omega : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega] {P : Measure Omega}
    (M : Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega P) :
    (∀ t : ℝ≥0, Measurable (M.markedProcess.observedCount t)) ∧
      (∀ᵐ omega ∂P, M.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) ∧
      (∀ᵐ omega ∂P,
        Monotone fun t => M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M.markedProcess.observedCount P ∧
      ∀ {s t : ℝ≥0}, s ≤ t → ∀ observedCount : ℕ,
        P.real {omega : Omega |
          M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -
            M.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =
          countLikelihood
            (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate
              M.incidentRate M.reportingRate M.durationDensity)
            ((t : ℝ) - (s : ℝ)) observedCount := by
  refine ⟨M.markedProcess.observedCount_measurable,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_zero_ae,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_mono_ae,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_hasIndepIncrements, ?_⟩
  intro s t hst observedCount
  simpa [continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate,
    M.latent_rate_eq_incidentRate,
    M.retention_probability_eq_firstReportProbability] using
    M.markedProcess.observedIntervalCount_mass_eq_countLikelihood hst observedCount

    (durationDensity : ℝ → ℝ)
    (durationDensity_source :
      ContinuousDurationDensitySourceCondition durationDensity)
    {observedRate : ℝ}
    (observedRate_pos : 0 < observedRate)
    (retention_one_pos :
      0 < continuousDurationFirstReportProbability 1 durationDensity)
    (retention_two_pos :
      0 < continuousDurationFirstReportProbability 2 durationDensity) :
    ∃ reportingRate1 reportingRate2 : ℝ,
      0 < reportingRate1 ∧
      0 < reportingRate2 ∧
      reportingRate1 ≠ reportingRate2 ∧
      ∃ (Omega1 : Type) (mOmega1 : MeasurableSpace Omega1) (P1 : Measure Omega1)
          (M1 : @Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega1 mOmega1 P1),
        ∃ (Omega2 : Type) (mOmega2 : MeasurableSpace Omega2) (P2 : Measure Omega2)
            (M2 : @Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega2 mOmega2 P2),
          M1.reportingRate = reportingRate1 ∧
          M2.reportingRate = reportingRate2 ∧
          M1.observedIncidentRate = observedRate ∧
          M2.observedIncidentRate = observedRate ∧
          (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1,
            Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
              (M1.observedUniqueIncidentCount n omega : ℝ) / n)
              atTop (nhds observedRate)) ∧
          (∀ᵐ omega ∂P2,
            Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
              (M2.observedUniqueIncidentCount n omega : ℝ) / n)
              atTop (nhds observedRate)) ∧
          ((∀ t : ℝ≥0, Measurable (M1.markedProcess.observedCount t)) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1, M1.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) ∧
            (∀ᵐ omega ∂P1,
              Monotone fun t => M1.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) ∧
            ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M1.markedProcess.observedCount P1 ∧
            ∀ {s t : ℝ≥0}, s ≤ t → ∀ observedCount : ℕ,
              P1.real {omega : Omega1 |
                M1.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -
                  M1.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =
                countLikelihood
                  (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate
                    M1.incidentRate M1.reportingRate M1.durationDensity)

theorem lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_observed_process
    {Omega : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Omega] {P : Measure Omega}
    (M : Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel Omega P) :
    (∀ t : ℝ≥0, Measurable (M.markedProcess.observedCount t)) ∧
      (∀ᵐ omega ∂P, M.markedProcess.observedCount 0 omega = 0) ∧
      (∀ᵐ omega ∂P,
        Monotone fun t => M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega) ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.HasIndepIncrements M.markedProcess.observedCount P ∧
      ∀ {s t : ℝ≥0}, s ≤ t → ∀ observedCount : ℕ,
        P.real {omega : Omega |
          M.markedProcess.observedCount t omega -
            M.markedProcess.observedCount s omega = observedCount} =
          countLikelihood
            (continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate
              M.incidentRate M.reportingRate M.durationDensity)
            ((t : ℝ) - (s : ℝ)) observedCount := by
  refine ⟨M.markedProcess.observedCount_measurable,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_zero_ae,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_mono_ae,
    M.markedProcess.observedCount_hasIndepIncrements, ?_⟩
  intro s t hst observedCount
  simpa [continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate,
    M.latent_rate_eq_incidentRate,
    M.retention_probability_eq_firstReportProbability] using
    M.markedProcess.observedIntervalCount_mass_eq_countLikelihood hst observedCount

model_conventions.checked_scope: assumption_lemma2_condition_one_selection exposes the measurable first-report/start/tail maps, one Markov conditional start kernel, its support after the first report, its conditional law, and conditional tail independence. The Lemma 2 source theorem derives the stated exponential tail from that condition and a constructed forward Poisson process. The exact ten recursive field paths below are the only convention-credit routes; the source-model container and unrelated witness fields receive no inherited credit.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's pointwise conditional-density notation for S given the continuously valued first report is represented by one rate-free regular conditional start kernel. Its support begins at the first report and it is conditionally independent of the supplied post-first-report tail; the fixed-history g(s) factor is separately rate independent.
model_conventions.why_needed: A literal probability P(S=t | T1=t1) is not a well-typed point-mass formula on a continuous carrier. Treating it as an unconditional scalar or as an arbitrary tail-dependent selector would lose the source's conditional and future-path independence content.

model_conventions.checked_scope: SourceTheoremModels.AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel exposes only a selected-start likelihood and visible-prefix endpoint kernels with measurability and nonnegative remaining-time support. CausalStoppingEndpointTrace constructs one endpoint from that policy, and PaperInterface.appendix_theorem2_eq8_causal_stopping_source_model derives the rate-free residual times the Poisson count PMF. The exact three endpoint-policy leaves below, and no density-presentation or container fields, receive this convention's source credit.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Theorem 1's endpoint condition is read as one rate-free causal stopping policy: after a visible report prefix, its conditional endpoint-response law may use that prefix but cannot inspect a future report gap. The selected-start contribution is conditioned on the pre-start history and is rate free. A canonical finite trace samples one terminal endpoint, rather than a global family of independently resampled counterfactual endpoint clocks.
model_conventions.why_needed: The Appendix's terse final independence display can be misread as only a marginal statement after T1. The main theorem explicitly conditions on reports observed up to the endpoint and the application calls its end rule a stopping-times assumption. The live-history reading preserves those source semantics and is the minimum policy content needed for the likelihood calculation.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The endpoint kernel is primary in AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel. EndpointDensityPresentation is an explicit AC presentation with a checked kernel-with-density equality. The canonical endpoint-law construction is atom safe, while the PaperInterface Eq. (8) theorem checks the scalar density factorization in exactly the source display's branch. Only the exact three density-presentation leaves below receive this convention's source credit; endpoint-policy and carrier fields do not.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's h_m(e) point-density notation is the absolutely-continuous presentation of an endpoint kernel. A deterministic cap or stopping endpoint can have an atom, so the general source model is a kernel law; the displayed scalar likelihood uses the explicitly supplied density presentation when the relevant endpoint branch is absolutely continuous.
model_conventions.why_needed: Treating every endpoint as Lebesgue-density-valued would silently exclude the fixed-cap observation policies described in the source application. Conversely, treating a point-density equation as a literal atom probability would not be a valid continuous likelihood statement.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel binds a genuine source duration density and the explicitly audited source p bridge to MarkedPoissonReportingProcess, whose fields are the latent process, mark probability, independent marked increments, and exact joint interval PMF. Its theorems derive the observed Poisson process and strong law; proposition1_steady_state_duration_source_exists_nonidentifiability selects 1 and 2 and constructs two positive-rate source models with equal derived observed rate under the explicit positive-retention condition. The exact nineteen nested/direct leaves below are the convention-credit routes; `retention_probability_eq_firstReportProbability` is the anchored duration-to-mark bridge, not a conclusion-bearing field. They do not credit the model container, rate witnesses, or unlisted process fields.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The duration/report-path model is represented at the level used by the source proof: a genuine probability density on [0,infinity), together with an iid eventual-report mark independent across latent incident increments. The explicit duration-to-mark bridge equates that mark probability with the source duration-mixture first-report integral. It is an audited source-model premise because the interface abstracts the lower-level per-incident report paths; it is not an observed-process conclusion or certificate. The latent incident process and the exact joint Poisson/Binomial marked interval law are primitive; the observed process, its independent increments, and the large-time law are derived. The source-facing nonidentifiability branch selects reporting rates 1 and 2 rather than accepting distinct rates as an unexplained premise.
model_conventions.why_needed: A generic structure named a marked process would be insufficient if it simply stored the observed Poisson conclusion or hid the retention probability. The source proof explicitly calculates p from a duration probability density and then invokes Binomial thinning, so the density-law condition, audited duration-to-mark bridge, and process evidence must remain visible in the model while the displayed observed-process conclusion is constructed by Lean. The bridge is a stated source semantic premise, not an unfilled proof obligation claimed as a theorem. Positive retention at the selected rates is explicit because compensating incident rates divide by p.

model_conventions.checked_scope: assumption_lemma2_condition_one_selection exposes the measurable first-report/start/tail maps, one Markov conditional start kernel, its support after the first report, its conditional law, and conditional tail independence. model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's pointwise conditional-density notation for S given the continuously valued first report is represented by one rate-free regular conditional start kernel. Its support begins at the first report and it is conditionally independent of the supplied post-first-report tail; the fixed-history g(s) factor is separately rate independent.
model_conventions.why_needed: A literal probability P(S=t | T1=t1) is not a well-typed point-mass formula on a continuous carrier. Treating it as an unconditional scalar or as an arbitrary tail-dependent selector would lose the source's conditional and future-path independence content.

model_conventions.checked_scope: SourceTheoremModels.AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel exposes only a selected-start likelihood and visible-prefix endpoint kernels with measurability and nonnegative remaining-time support. CausalStoppingEndpointTrace constructs one endpoint from that policy, and PaperInterface.appendix_theorem2_eq8_causal_stopping_source_model derives the rate-free residual times the Poisson count PMF. The exact three endpoint-policy leaves below, and no density-presentation or container fields, receive this convention's source credit.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Theorem 1's endpoint condition is read as one rate-free causal stopping policy: after a visible report prefix, its conditional endpoint-response law may use that prefix but cannot inspect a future report gap. The selected-start contribution is conditioned on the pre-start history and is rate free. A canonical finite trace samples one terminal endpoint, rather than a global family of independently resampled counterfactual endpoint clocks.
model_conventions.why_needed: The Appendix's terse final independence display can be misread as only a marginal statement after T1. The main theorem explicitly conditions on reports observed up to the endpoint and the application calls its end rule a stopping-times assumption. The live-history reading preserves those source semantics and is the minimum policy content needed for the likelihood calculation.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The endpoint kernel is primary in AppendixTheorem2CausalStoppingSourceModel. EndpointDensityPresentation is an explicit AC presentation with a checked kernel-with-density equality. The canonical endpoint-law construction is atom safe, while the PaperInterface Eq. (8) theorem checks the scalar density factorization in exactly the source display's branch. Only the exact three density-presentation leaves below receive this convention's source credit; endpoint-policy and carrier fields do not.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's h_m(e) point-density notation is the absolutely-continuous presentation of an endpoint kernel. A deterministic cap or stopping endpoint can have an atom, so the general source model is a kernel law; the displayed scalar likelihood uses the explicitly supplied density presentation when the relevant endpoint branch is absolutely continuous.
model_conventions.why_needed: Treating every endpoint as Lebesgue-density-valued would silently exclude the fixed-cap observation policies described in the source application. Conversely, treating a point-density equation as a literal atom probability would not be a valid continuous likelihood statement.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Lemma1SteadyStateDurationSourceModel binds a genuine source duration density and the explicitly audited source p bridge to MarkedPoissonReportingProcess, whose fields are the latent process, mark probability, independent marked increments, and exact joint interval PMF. Its theorems derive the observed Poisson process and strong law; proposition1_steady_state_duration_source_exists_nonidentifiability selects 1 and 2 and constructs two positive-rate source models with equal derived observed rate under the explicit positive-retention condition. The exact nineteen nested/direct leaves below are the convention-credit routes; `retention_probability_eq_firstReportProbability` is the anchored duration-to-mark bridge, not a conclusion-bearing field. They do not credit the model container, rate witnesses, or unlisted process fields.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The duration/report-path model is represented at the level used by the source proof: a genuine probability density on [0,infinity), together with an iid eventual-report mark independent across latent incident increments. The explicit duration-to-mark bridge equates that mark probability with the source duration-mixture first-report integral. It is an audited source-model premise because the interface abstracts the lower-level per-incident report paths; it is not an observed-process conclusion or certificate. The latent incident process and the exact joint Poisson/Binomial marked interval law are primitive; the observed process, its independent increments, and the large-time law are derived. The source-facing nonidentifiability branch selects reporting rates 1 and 2 rather than accepting distinct rates as an unexplained premise.
model_conventions.why_needed: A generic structure named a marked process would be insufficient if it simply stored the observed Poisson conclusion or hid the retention probability. The source proof explicitly calculates p from a duration probability density and then invokes Binomial thinning, so the density-law condition, audited duration-to-mark bridge, and process evidence must remain visible in the model while the displayed observed-process conclusion is constructed by Lean. The bridge is a stated source semantic premise, not an unfilled proof obligation claimed as a theorem. Positive retention at the selected rates is explicit because compensating incident rates divide by p.
